content: Pain is a commonly reported symptom. Nervous/Psychiatric System: Patients have experienced a reduction in libido, episodes of vertigo, depressive symptoms, and excessive drowsiness (somnolence). Respiratory System: Reported conditions include the common cold, nasal congestion, influenza, bronchitis, pharyngeal pain, shortness of breath (dyspnea), pulmonary congestion, chronic sinusitis, allergic rhinitis, and discomfort in the pharyngeal region. Skin: Adverse reactions affecting the skin include flushing, itching (pruritus), skin inflammation, excessive sweating (diaphoresis), and a rare condition known as cutaneous pseudolymphoma. Special Senses: Patients have reported blurred vision, ringing in the ears (tinnitus), and ear pain (otalgia). Urogenital System: Urinary tract infections have been observed. Angioedema: Cases of angioedema involving the face, extremities, lips, tongue, glottis, and/or larynx have been reported. Intestinal angioedema has also been documented in rare instances during post-marketing surveillance. Cough: Cough has been noted as a potential adverse effect (refer to precautions regarding cough). Clinical Laboratory Test Findings: Serum Electrolytes: Abnormalities in serum electrolytes have been observed (refer to precautions). Creatinine and Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN): Minor, reversible increases in BUN and serum creatinine levels have been noted in patients with essential hypertension treated with lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. More significant increases have been reported, particularly in patients with renal artery stenosis (refer to precautions). Serum Uric Acid, Glucose, Magnesium, Cholesterol, Triglycerides, and Calcium: Changes in these parameters have been observed but are rarely of clinical significance unless another cause of anemia coexists. Approximately 4% of patients discontinued therapy due to anemia. Liver Function Tests: Rare elevations in liver enzymes and/or serum bilirubin have been reported (refer to warnings regarding hepatic failure). Other Adverse Reactions: Lisinopril: Adverse reactions observed in clinical trials with lisinopril were also seen with the combination of lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. These include paresthesia, dysesthesia, muscle spasms, hypersomnia, irritability, and mood alterations (including depressive symptoms). Respiratory System: Malignant lung neoplasms, coughing up blood (hemoptysis), pulmonary edema, pulmonary infiltrates, bronchospasm, asthma, pleural effusion, pneumonia, eosinophilic pneumonitis, wheezing, difficulty breathing while lying down (orthopnea), painful respiration, nosebleeds (epistaxis), laryngitis, sinusitis, pharyngitis, rhinitis, nasal discharge (rhinorrhea), and abnormal chest sounds have been reported. Skin: Skin-related adverse effects include hives (urticaria), hair loss (alopecia), herpes zoster, photosensitivity, skin lesions, skin infections, pemphigus, erythema, psoriasis, and rare severe skin reactions such as toxic epidermal necrolysis and Stevens-Johnson syndrome (causal relationship not established). Special Senses: Visual loss, double vision (diplopia), sensitivity to light (photophobia), taste alterations, and olfactory disturbances have been reported. Urogenital System: Acute renal failure, reduced urine output (oliguria), absence of urine production (anuria), uremia, progressive azotemia, renal dysfunction (refer to precautions and dosage/administration), kidney infection (pyelonephritis), painful urination (dysuria), and breast pain have been documented.
